newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at 8.2999 against the U.S. dollar on Monday on a technical correction from last Friday's 8.2985, with no impact seen from the truce in the Sino-U.S. trade war, traders said.
The official Chinese media reported that China had decided to suspend a ban on imports of American goods, which had originally been scheduled to be implemented on from Tuesday.
Dealers said the news, which has big significance for Sino-American trade and many China's export-oriented firms, had no direct influence on the yuan's movement.
The yuan opened lower at 8.2999 and consolidated around 8.2995 for most of the session, hitting an intra-day high of 8.2990 and a low of 8.3003.
Trading was active, with most done at 8.2998, traders said.
"If China really stops imports of some goods from the U.S., the demand for dollars will fall to some extent and the yuan will find strong support," one dealer said.
"But this is not expected to happen," he added.
"Today's fall was mainly a technical correction," a second dealer said. "The yuan needed a correction after closing at a three-week high last Friday."
"But active buying ahead the year-end helped it to stand above the key 8.3000 level today," he added.
Dealers expect the yuan to move around 8.3000 on Tuesday.
The yuan closed down slightly at an intra-day low of 7.3700 from 7.3513 against 100 Japanese yen and was unchanged at 1.0740 against the Hong Kong dollar.
